A new look, Tidelight. Today opens under a sky that follows the clock: misty at dawn, clear through the day, golden at dusk and deep teal at night. Light and dark still follow your setting.

The sun on Today's arc moves as you log food and sets at your target. Each meal lights its own piece of the arc, and the big number is what's left. Going over sets the sun with a soft glow, never red.

Your day reads as a timeline: what you ate, when, and its protein, each with its own slice of the arc. Tap an entry to edit it; touch and hold to repeat, add a photo or delete. When there's room, your usual next meal sits on the Now line, one tap from logging.

The week strip at the top of Today shows how each day went, and the This week row says what's banked and what the rest of the week can have. Protein leads the macros, and once your calories are spent it stops telling you to eat more.

Week is seven skies, filled to each day's target, with a running balance line and a plain answer for the days left. Details, averages and how the bank works are one tap away. The tab bar now floats; + logs food from any tab, and Settings is the sliders button on Today.
On wider phones like the Pro Max, the sky on Today and Week now reaches the edges of the screen, with no pale strip down each side or band under the clock.
Log with AI is back near the top of Today: one button opens Estimate with Gemini, Help me pick from a menu, and copy/paste for other chatbots. The + button is now just for typing a food in yourself.
